title: Coral and the Compass
premise: Tamsin Winterbourne, a riverboat captain who has spent two decades dodging debts, lawmen, and her own past, is handed a dying prospector's map to the river's forbidden source along with a promise to deliver it to his daughter in the high country. Pursued by the prospector's former partners—who will kill for the map—and shadowed by Coral, a government surveyor sent to chart the very territory Tamsin has spent years keeping off every map, Tamsin must choose between the loyalty she owes the dead man and the truth Coral keeps pressing her to face. As the dry season lowers the river and betrayal strikes from within their small crew, Tamsin and Coral fall in love even as duty pulls them toward opposite answers. In the end, Tamsin reaches the source, gives the map to the daughter, and burns it—choosing love and truth over survival by invisibility, and steering her boat back downriver with Coral aboard.
about_author: Theo Voss is a former deckhand turned novelist who spent six seasons working freight on inland waterways before trading the wheelhouse for a writing desk. Known for adventure fiction steeped in river lore, Voss writes about people who measure their lives in miles rather than years.

chapters.title: The Dying Man's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A fevered prospector collapses aboard at a fueling dock and trades Tamsin a hand-drawn map to the river's source for a promise: carry it upstream to his daughter before the dry season ends. Tamsin accepts against her instincts. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion cracking open a carefully sealed life.

chapters.title: Passenger with a Government Seal
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the next landing, Coral Ashford boards—a surveyor commissioned to chart the upper river, the one region Tamsin has spent twenty years keeping blank on official maps. Coral is sharp-eyed, polite, and dangerous. Emotional beat: wary attraction laced with the dread of being truly seen.

chapters.title: Men Who Smell of Gunpowder
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Two strangers press the crew for news of a missing prospector; Coral recognizes them as claim-jumpers from her own files but says nothing, torn between duty and suspicion of Tamsin. That night she finds Tamsin studying the map by lamplight. Emotional beat: the first fracture between loyalty and truth.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The dry season begins early; sandbars shift and the boat grounds hard in a narrows while the pursuers close from behind. The crew hauls her free through the night, and Coral works beside them without being asked. Emotional beat: grudging respect hardening into trust—and the cost of the journey made physical.

chapters.title: What the Daughter Sent
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A letter from the prospector's daughter reaches them via river post, revealing the old man was murdered for his claim and naming his killers' faces—faces Coral knows. She hides the letter from Tamsin. Emotional beat: guilt taking root; love beginning despite deception.

chapters.title: The First Betrayal
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A trusted crew member sells their position to the claim-jumpers for amnesty and slips away with half their supplies. Ambushed at a bend, they escape only by running rapids no sane pilot would attempt—with Coral reading the water aloud from the stolen charts. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into intimacy; the price of survival counted in blood and gear.

chapters.title: Where the Maps End
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Above the last surveyed reach, the river turns wild and beautiful. Coral confesses her commission and her hidden letter; Tamsin confesses the map and the promise. They fight, then stand watch together under stars no chart records. Emotional beat: raw honesty after betrayal—love chosen knowingly, against duty.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. They abandon the grounded boat and climb to the source: a spring rising cold and silver from living rock, guarded by an abandoned claim camp and the daughter waiting there, armed and grieving. The claim-jumpers arrive at dusk. Emotional beat: awe curdling into siege—the endgame begun.

chapters.title: Cold Water Rising
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The final confrontation at the spring: the crew holds the high ground through the night, Coral turns her survey evidence over to the daughter to legally destroy the jumpers' claim, and Tamsin takes a bullet graze shielding the map. Emotional beat: climax—loyalty, truth, and love all demanded at once, and paid.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The daughter burns the map herself, freeing Tamsin from the promise; the jumpers are taken by the river law Coral summoned. Repaired and lighter, the boat starts home with Coral aboard—not as surveyor, but as crew. Emotional beat: resolution—invisibility traded for a shared future, life measured finally in years, not miles.
